name: Taj Mahal
overview: The Taj Mahal is a white-marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna River in Agra. Commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan after the death of his wife Mumtaz Mahal in 1631, it is widely regarded as the finest expression of Mughal architecture, which fuses Persian, Islamic and Indian traditions. The complex is more than the tomb: it includes a monumental gateway, a formal charbagh garden, a mosque and a matching guest house, all arranged on a strict axis. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 under criterion (i) as a masterpiece of human creative genius. Its symmetry, proportions and the way the marble shifts colour from dawn to dusk draw millions of visitors every year.
history: [400-700 words: Mumtaz Mahal's death at Burhanpur in 1631 -> site selection and land exchange -> construction start 1632 -> Ustad Ahmad Lahori and the workforce of ~20,000 -> marble from Makrana, materials from across Asia -> mausoleum substantially complete c.1648, complex c.1653 -> Shah Jahan's deposition by Aurangzeb and burial beside Mumtaz -> colonial-era neglect, Lord Curzon's restoration (1900s) -> ASI protection, pollution control zone (Taj Trapezium) -> UNESCO 1983.]
architecture: [300-500 words: raised plinth, central onion dome ~35 m, four minarets (slightly tilted outward), pishtaq arches, double-dome construction, charbagh quadrants, pietra dura, calligraphy with perspective scaling, red sandstone mosque & jawab, Yamuna riverfront terrace.]
cultural_significance: [200-350 words: symbol of love and of India; Mughal court culture; Parchin Kari craft survival in Agra; role in tourism and national identity; living craft community.]
